title: cli-resume: Wire cmd_resume to lifecycle::resume (currently no-op)
description: Bug P0-3. lifecycle::resume at crates/vb_cli/src/lifecycle.rs:150-220 is fully implemented (opens Fjall, validates the run is suspended with a valid suspended_at_step, then enqueues ShardCommand::Resume with the step). But run_ops.rs:100-156 (cmd_resume) only calls commands_journal::analyze_resume (pure read-only) and returns. analyze_resume (commands_journal.rs:386-429) sets can_resume: true whenever the run is non-terminal, which is wrong: a non-terminal run that is not actually suspended (no suspended_at_step) cannot be resumed, and the current logic allows that no-op. Master §33.3 (Lifecycle Command Surface) lists resume as a first-class command. This bead: (1) imports crate::lifecycle in run_ops.rs and calls lifecycle::resume after analyze_resume confirms can_resume: true AND suspended_at_step.is_some(); (2) fixes analyze_resume to require suspended_at_step.is_some() before setting can_resume: true.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL emit a JournalEvent::RunResumed when cmd_resume is invoked on a suspended run
THE SYSTEM SHALL reject resume of a non-suspended run with a typed NotSuspended error

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user runs `vb resume <run-id> --db <path>` on a run with suspended_at_step: Some(step)
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL open the Fjall journal, call lifecycle::resume, and append JournalEvent::RunResumed

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user runs `vb resume <run-id> --db <path>` on a run with suspended_at_step: None
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 3 with NotSuspended and write nothing to the journal

unwanted.condition: IF cmd_resume is called on a terminal run (RunFinished, RunFailed, RunCancelled, RunRetried)
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT silently succeed; it must return a typed TerminalRunNotResumable error
unwanted.because: Terminal runs are immutable from the runtime's perspective; silent no-op hides operator confusion

unwanted.condition: IF cmd_resume is called with a run id for a run that has no suspended steps
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT enqueue a ShardCommand::Resume that no-ops in the shard loop
unwanted.because: Wastes a shard tick and pollutes the trace with empty Resume events

preconditions: Run exists in the Fjall journal at the supplied --db path
Run is in a non-terminal state
Run has at least one step in StepState::Waiting or StepState::Asking (suspended_at_step is Some)
postconditions: JournalEvent::RunResumed is appended with the original run_id and the suspended step index
ShardCommand::Resume(run_id, suspended_at_step) is enqueued to the run's owning shard
invariants: Resume is the inverse of suspension; suspended_at_step preserves the exact step boundary (master §68.4: recovery is deterministic)
cmd_resume never resumes a step that has already advanced past suspended_at_step (idempotency check at shard)

happy: cli_resume_after_wait_until_writes_run_resumed_event: submit a workflow with a WaitUntil step, wait for the timer to expire (or use vb timer-fire), then `vb resume <id> --db /tmp/db`; journal contains JournalEvent::RunResumed with the WaitUntil step
cli_resume_preserves_waiting_step_state: after resume, the previously Waiting step transitions to Succeeded and pc advances
error: cli_resume_after_finished_run_returns_terminal_error: finish a run, then resume; exits 3 with TerminalRunNotResumable
cli_resume_on_running_run_with_no_suspended_step_returns_not_suspended: run a fast workflow that never suspends, then resume; exits 3 with NotSuspended
edge: cli_resume_after_cancellation_returns_terminal_error: cancel a suspended run, then resume; exits 3 (terminal trumps suspended)

crates/vb_cli/src/run_ops.rs:100-156 (cmd_resume function; needs the import + call)
patterns: Pattern: existing `use crate::lifecycle;` import (none yet; P0-2 will add the first one for retry)
Pattern: analyze_resume returns AnalyzeResult { can_resume: bool, suspended_at_step: Option<StepIdx>, reason: String }
questions: Should the suspended_at_step check be a separate variant of AnalyzeResult or part of can_resume logic? (Spec: separate; can_resume is for terminal-vs-not, suspended_at_step gate the actual call.)
Does lifecycle::resume need a NotSuspended error variant, or is the existing CliError::InvalidRunState enough? (Spec: add a typed NotSuspended for clarity.)

security_failures.failure: Operator resumes a run with a corrupted journal record, advancing past a step that should have failed
security_failures.prevention: lifecycle::resume must verify the digest of the WorkflowSourceRecord before enqueuing Resume (defense in depth)

usability_failures.failure: Operator runs `vb resume` on a run that has no `vb inspect` output to confirm suspension; gets an opaque error
usability_failures.prevention: NotSuspended error message includes a hint: 'Use `vb events <id>` to inspect the last event; resume requires a Waiting or Asking step'

data_integrity_failures.failure: Resume advances the run past suspended_at_step but the journal lacks the corresponding StepSucceeded event
data_integrity_failures.prevention: lifecycle::resume writes a StepResumed placeholder event before enqueuing; recovery can use it as a marker

integration_failures.failure: Resume enqueues to the wrong shard, leaving the run suspended indefinitely
integration_failures.prevention: lifecycle::resume reads run_header.owning_shard and enqueues to that exact shard (shard routing is mandatory per master §20)

In commands/journal.rs:386-429 analyze_resume, add a check: if suspended_at_step.is_none(), return AnalyzeResult { can_resume: false, suspended_at_step: None, reason: 'No suspended step; cannot resume' }
